properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 14 at 7:38AM CDT by NWS Aberdeen SD
properties.description:
At 738 AM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a line of strong
thunderstorms extending from over Gettysburg to over Harrold, or
extending from over Gettysburg to 13 miles east of Blunt, moving
northeast at 40 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

The strong thunderstorm will be near...
Stone Lake, Gettysburg, Harrold and Cottonwood Lake Near Agar
around 740 AM CDT.
Holabird around 745 AM CDT.
Lebanon around 755 AM CDT.
Seneca around 805 AM CDT.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued September 14 at 6:32AM MDT until September 14 at 8:45AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows are possible, flooding
caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern Ouray County in southwestern Colorado from
Ouray to Portland over the Gold Mountain burn scar.

* WHEN...Until 845 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall is possible over the Gold Mountain
Burn Scar which could lead to flash flooding and/or debris flows,
particularly along highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter
Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 632 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in Gold Mountain Burn Scar.
- Gold Mountain Burn Scar is the most likely place to experience
minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Ouray.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Climb to higher ground. Avoid Cutler and Dexter Creek drainages.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued September 14 at 7:27AM CDT until September 14 at 1:30PM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO
properties.description:
FFWEAX

The National Weather Service in Pleasant Hill has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Daviess County in north central Missouri...
Southwestern Harrison County in north central Missouri...
Northern DeKalb County in northwestern Missouri...
Southern Gentry County in northwestern Missouri...

* Until 130 PM CDT Monday.

* At 727 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 1.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
King City, Pattonsburg, Mcfall and Ford City.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
properties.area: Daviess, MO; DeKalb, MO; Gentry, MO; Harrison, MO

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 14 at 6:44AM CDT by NWS Aberdeen SD
properties.description:
At 644 AM CDT /544 AM MDT/, Doppler radar was tracking a line of
strong thunderstorms extending from 7 miles north of Herreid to over
Lebanon, or extending from 7 miles north of Herreid to 10 miles
northeast of Gettysburg, moving northeast at 55 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph and half inch size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

The strong thunderstorm will be near...
Hoven, Lebanon, Herreid and Java around 645 AM CDT.
Artas and Bowdle around 650 AM CDT.
Greenway, Tolstoy and Eureka around 655 AM CDT.
Hillsview and Onaka around 700 AM CDT.
Hosmer around 705 AM CDT.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead
to flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.
properties.area: Corson; Campbell; McPherson; Walworth; Edmunds; Potter; Faulk; Sully

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued September 14 at 6:43AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Coastal Waters from Southwest Pass of the Mississippi River to Port
Fourchon LA out 20 nm...
Coastal Waters from Boothville LA to Southwest Pass of the
Mississippi River out 20 nm...

* At 643 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots and weak waterspouts.
These strong thunderstorms were located along a line from 15 NM
northwest of Southwest Pass Of the Mississippi River to 23 NM east
of Pilottown, moving south at 5 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Southwest Pass Of the Mississippi River.
properties.instruction:
Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, weak waterspouts,
locally higher waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe
harbor immediately until these storms pass.
properties.area: Coastal waters from the Southwest Pass of the Mississippi River to Port Fourchon Louisiana out 20 NM; Coastal Waters from Boothville LA to Southwest Pass of the Mississippi River out 20 nm

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued September 14 at 5:42AM MDT until September 14 at 7:45AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Ferris Burn Scar in...
Northwestern Dolores County in southwestern Colorado...

* Until 745 AM MDT.

* At 542 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated several rounds of
thunderstorms producing moderate to heavy rainfall rates over the
Ferris Burn Scar. Between 0.2 and 0.5 inches of rain have fallen.
The expected rainfall rate is 0.7 to 1.5 inches in 1 hour. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Excessive
rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow. The debris
flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Ferris Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Ferris Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Areas in and near the Ferris burn scar of Northwestern Dolores
County.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Ferris Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 14 at 5:18AM EDT until September 14 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Boston/Norton MA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Norton has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Rhode Island...

Wood River At Hope Valley affecting Washington County.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 200 PM EDT.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Wood River at Hope Valley.

* WHEN...From early this morning to this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 5.0 feet, In Richmond, floodwaters begin to pond onto
Wood River Drive. In Hopkinton off of Main Street, the Wood River
begins to flood Dow Park.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:15 AM EDT Monday the stage was 5.1 feet. The river will be
near or just above flood stage this morning before dropping below
flood stage this afternoon.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:15 AM EDT Monday was 5.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 2.1 feet Wednesday
evening.
- Flood stage is 5.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 5.1
feet on 01/27/1952.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
